thesis: The site's primary conversion mechanism is the coverage-check form, but it is undermined by multiple competing CTAs and ambiguous form labels, causing visitors to hesitate or abandon before entering their address. Consolidating to a single, clearly labeled coverage-check CTA and form will directly increase conversion.

findings.title: Competing CTAs
findings.summary: Multiple competing CTAs on the homepage and all pages create ambiguity about which path to take, diluting the primary conversion action.
findings.problem: Multiple different CTAs all leading to the same coverage check create ambiguity about which path to take.
findings.recommended_change: cta: One primary CTA for coverage check, secondary actions de-emphasized.; notes: Consolidate coverage-check CTAs into one primary action with a single label.
findings.evidence: CHECK COVERAGE | CHECK IF IT WORKS AT MY ADDRESS | SEE MY OPTIONS | GET STARTED | START CHAT | SEE WHAT I QUALIFY FOR | CHECK MY COVERAGE
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 2.0-8.0% relative lift

findings.title: Weak page metadata
findings.summary: Search and social previews are degraded: meta description, Open Graph tags are missing or outside recommended lengths.
findings.problem: Search and social previews are degraded: meta description, Open Graph tags are missing or outside recommended lengths.
findings.recommended_change: notes: Write a 15-60 char title and 70-160 char description per page; add og:title and og:image for link previews.
findings.evidence: Measured on the homepage: title 17 chars (15-60 recommended); description 0 chars (70-160 recommended); og:title missing, og:image missing.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 0.5-2.0% relative lift

findings.title: Unclear form field labels
findings.summary: The coverage-check forms present five fields each, but the page digest does not reveal what information is requested, so visitors cannot tell what they need to enter.
findings.problem: The coverage-check forms present five fields each, but the page digest does not reveal what information is requested, so visitors cannot tell what they need to enter.
findings.recommended_change: cta: CONTINUE; notes: Ensure each of the five form fields has a visible, descriptive label.
findings.evidence: form: submit=CONTINUE (field extraction is unreliable on this site — raw HTML carries 5 field(s); do not claim fields or labels are missing)
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 1.0-5.0% relative lift

findings.title: Social proof isolated
findings.summary: Customer testimonials appear only on the homepage and rural-internet page, while the plans pages where users choose a plan and price show no reviews or social proof.
findings.problem: Customer testimonials appear only on the homepage and rural-internet page, while the plans pages where users choose a plan and price show no reviews or social proof.
findings.recommended_change: notes: Add customer testimonials or review snippets to the plans pages near pricing and coverage CTAs.

findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 1.0-5.0% relative lift

findings.title: Ambiguous next step
findings.summary: After coverage check, the funnel's next step is unclear due to multiple h1 questions and several CTAs without a clear sequence.
findings.problem: After coverage check, the funnel's next step is unclear due to multiple h1 questions and several CTAs without a clear sequence.
findings.recommended_change: h1: One clear question per page; cta: One primary CTA that advances to next step; notes: Structure funnel so each page has one clear question and one primary CTA.
